about: India measured on the metrics Dan Wang's Breakneck uses for China and the United States. Each India figure is cited to the publisher it was read from. 'comparable' says how far the India number measures the same thing as the book's: direct (same measure), approximate (close, with a stated difference) or context (a different measure, shown for orientation only). Figures from the World Bank are not repeated here; the page reads them from data/series/wdi.json.

india.label: Cities with an operating metro, March 2026
Cities with an operating metro, May 2025

metrics.note: India's count includes elevated and light-metro lines; the book counts Chinese cities with subways. The government describes India's network as the world's third-largest by length.

metrics.note: India's first line is shorter than either line the book compares, and like California's is a promise rather than a service. Opening dates are official targets, not achievements.

metrics.title: Highways
metrics.note: India's national highways are mostly two- and four-lane roads, not access-controlled expressways like the US interstates or China's expressway network, so the lengths do not compare like for like.

metrics.title: Spending on building, as a share of GDP
metrics.note: Central government only, and a budget estimate: it leaves out states, public enterprises and private investment, and includes capital spending that is not infrastructure. It is not the book's measure; the World Bank's gross capital formation, shown alongside, is the closer like-for-like.

metrics.title: Factory workforce

india.label: Employed in registered factories, 2023–24 (Annual Survey of Industries)

metrics.note: The Annual Survey of Industries covers registered factories only. Most Indian manufacturing employment is in small unregistered workshops it does not count, so this understates India's manufacturing workforce.
